explainers.title: What is a freighter aircraft?
explainers.body: A freighter carries cargo on its main deck, where a passenger aircraft has its cabin, as well as in the holds below. It has a large cargo door on the main deck, a strengthened floor, a system for moving cargo around and a barrier between the cargo and the flight crew. Some freighters are built that way at the factory (production or purpose-built freighters). Others are converted from passenger aircraft (passenger-to-freighter, or P2F).

references.title: Boeing Freighters

explainers.basis: General explanation. The freighter examples are sourced.

explainers.title: What is passenger-to-freighter (P2F) conversion?
explainers.body: A P2F conversion turns a used passenger aircraft into a freighter. The cabin is stripped out. The fuselage is reinforced around a new main-deck cargo door, and the floor is rebuilt to take cargo loads. Windows and unused passenger doors are plugged or locked. Finally a rigid barrier, a cargo loading system and fire protection are fitted, so the main deck can be certified as a cargo compartment. The modified design is approved through a Supplemental Type Certificate (STC).

Conversion provider's public page on the A330P2F conversion

explainers.title: Why do operators convert passenger aircraft?
explainers.body: Passenger aircraft often have plenty of structural life left when they leave passenger service. Converting them provides freighter capacity for less than a new production freighter would cost. It also fills sizes that aren't built new as freighters, such as narrowbody freighters like the A321P2F. Conversion providers say these freighters serve the e-commerce, express and general cargo markets. There's no conversion cost data on this site, so no cost comparison is shown.

explainers.title: What is a main-deck cargo door?
explainers.body: The main-deck cargo door is a large opening in the side of the fuselage. Containers and pallets go through it onto the main deck, so its width and height decide the largest unit load device that fits. On the A321P2F the door is 142 in wide and 85 in high. On the A330P2F it is 141 in by 101 in.

references.title: Conversion provider's public page on the A320/A321P2F conversion
Conversion provider's public page on the A330P2F conversion

explainers.title: What are ULDs and cargo pallets?
explainers.body: Unit load devices (ULDs) are the containers and pallets that bundle many shipments into one unit, which can be loaded quickly and locked to the floor. Containers are shaped to follow the curve of the fuselage: AAY containers on the A321P2F main deck, for example, and AKH or LD3 containers in lower decks. Pallets are flat platforms with nets, in sizes such as 96 × 125 in. IATA publishes the ULD regulations.

references.title: Unit Load Devices (ULD)
Conversion provider's public page on the A320/A321P2F conversion

explainers.title: What is a cargo loading system?
explainers.body: The cargo loading system (CLS) is the equipment in the floor that lets ground staff move ULDs from the door to their positions and lock them down. It's made up of roller tracks, ball mats near the door, side guides and locks. In a powered system (PCLS), drive units move the containers. The A330P2F conversion has a powered loading system in which containers are power-driven into position.

explainers.title: How do payload and range interact?
explainers.body: With a full payload the aircraft is at its maximum zero-fuel weight (MZFW), so it can only take on as much fuel as still fits under MTOW. That fuel sets the range at maximum payload. To fly further, some payload has to come off so more fuel can go in, until the tanks are full. Boeing's published figures show the trade-off: 5,000 nmi with a 107-tonne payload for the 777F, and 3,300 nmi with 57 tonnes for the 767-300F.

references.title: Boeing Freighters

explainers.basis: General explanation of the trade-off. The published payload and range figures are sourced.

explainers.title: How are converted freighters different from purpose-built freighters?
explainers.body: Production freighters are designed and certified as freighters from the start, with structure, doors and weights built for cargo, and they're built new. Converted freighters keep the passenger aircraft's original structure, with reinforcements added. So their empty weight, payload and limits differ both from the passenger version and from any production freighter in the same family. Boeing, for instance, offers both the 767-300 Freighter (production) and the 767-300 Boeing Converted Freighter. Figures for one must never be used for the other.

conversion_steps.title: Selecting the aircraft
conversion_steps.body: A suitable passenger aircraft is chosen, based on its type, weight variant and structural condition, and brought into the conversion facility. The A321P2F conversion's STC covers all weight variants of the A321-200.

references.title: Conversion provider's public page on the A320/A321P2F conversion

conversion_steps.title: Stripping the cabin
conversion_steps.body: Seats, galleys, toilets, overhead bins and cabin linings all come out, exposing the structure underneath.
conversion_steps.basis: General description. The cited pages don't describe this step.

conversion_steps.title: Rebuilding the floor
conversion_steps.body: The floor is rebuilt to carry cargo loads. For the A321P2F, the published description says the floor is rebuilt and that stringers and frames are replaced or reinforced.

references.title: Conversion provider's public page on the A320/A321P2F conversion
Conversion provider's public page on the A330P2F conversion

conversion_steps.title: Cutting in the cargo door
conversion_steps.body: A large opening is cut in the side of the fuselage and the main-deck cargo door is fitted. The fuselage around it is reinforced.

references.title: Conversion provider's public page on the A320/A321P2F conversion
Conversion provider's public page on the A330P2F conversion

conversion_steps.title: Closing windows and doors
conversion_steps.body: The windows are replaced with plugs and the rear passenger doors are locked shut.

references.title: Conversion provider's public page on the A330P2F conversion
Conversion provider's public page on the A320/A321P2F conversion

conversion_steps.title: Barrier, loading system and fire protection
conversion_steps.body: A rigid barrier is fitted to separate the crew from the cargo. On the A321P2F the barrier is designed for loads of up to 9 g. A cargo loading system and fire protection for a Class E cargo compartment go in as well.

references.title: Conversion provider's public page on the A320/A321P2F conversion
Conversion provider's public page on the A330P2F conversion

conversion_steps.title: Certification and handover
conversion_steps.body: The modification is approved through a Supplemental Type Certificate (STC). After testing, the aircraft is handed back as a freighter.
